chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from 'Urwa ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you meet the caravan of goods coming from outside the city [to buy from them before the others], and let not one who is present in the city sell to one who is in the countryside [by sending goods ahead], and the Muslims are partners in providing sustenance for one another.'

key_terms.بَاد: One who is in the countryside or remote area
key_terms.تِلْقَاء: Meeting the caravan/goods outside the city
key_terms.حَاضِر: One who is present (in the city)

ai.seo_question: What are the prohibited trade practices in Islam regarding meeting caravans and selling to those in the countryside?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the prohibition of 'iqd al-ghurra' (preemptive purchase) to prevent market manipulation and hoarding by wealthy merchants who intercept caravars before they reach the city market. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on economic justice and transparency, ensuring that goods are sold at fair market value rather than through speculative advantage, thereby fostering mutual sustenance among the community.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Urwa Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘You should not travel to meet the carvan of suppliers out of the city before other buyers’ One should not buy for the ones who are not present.  Allah<sup>azwj </sup>Grants sustenance to the Muslims through one another.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from ’Urwah ibn ‘ Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must not travel to meet the caravan of suppliers out of the city before other buyers. One must not buy for the ones who are not present. Allah grants sustenance to the Muslims through one another.”’
